page.title: Locking the airline seats
page.kicker: Lecture 03 · week 2, day 1 · running cases: airline check-in, a key-value store on MySQL
page.dek: See pessimistic locking work live on an airline check-in, then build a key-value store on top of MySQL.
page.description: Lecture 03: row locks, deadlocks and isolation; an airline check-in fixed by two SQL words at a time; a key-value store on MySQL where every clause has a cost; Redis expiry; replicas and range shards.

chapters.title: Locks, in theory
chapters.summary: Before coding the check-in, the tools: why relational databases are strict, shared and exclusive row locks, SKIP LOCKED and NOWAIT, deadlocks, isolation levels, and where a lock lives.

chapters.title: Building the airline check-in
chapters.summary: 120 passengers, 120 kiosks, one moment. Six versions of one program: four double-book, FOR UPDATE makes it correct, SKIP LOCKED makes it ten times faster.

chapters.title: A key-value store on MySQL
chapters.summary: GET, PUT, DELETE and per-key expiry on one table. Each operation starts with the obvious query and ends with a cheaper one.

chapters.title: If it were in memory: how Redis expires keys
chapters.summary: On disk you batch. In memory a delete is nearly free: delete on access, and sample twenty keys at a time for the rest.

chapters.title: Making it distributed
chapters.summary: Grow the single node one bottleneck at a time: more API servers, read replicas, range shards with routing in the API, and what happens to ACID.

chapters.title: Craft, opinions, and what to keep
chapters.summary: The instructor's views on ORMs, languages and learning, the heuristics from both builds, and where this lecture stops.
